coaching.summary: Three competing causal theories are each mapped to a separate option, but the decision currently lacks a way to test which theory is actually correct before committing resources this quarter.

strengthen_items.label: Add a diagnostic step as an explicit constraint
strengthen_items.detail: Because engineering, support, and product each hold a different causal theory, acting without first measuring which factor actually drove the volume spike risks spending the quarter on the wrong fix — a short triage sprint or ticket-tagging exercise could surface this before full commitment.

strengthen_items.label: Include a 'do nothing this quarter' option for comparison
strengthen_items.detail: The urgency framing ('we have to act this quarter') may be suppressing consideration of a deliberate delay option, which would make the cost of inaction explicit and sharpen the case for whichever active option is chosen.

strengthen_items.label: Surface team capacity as a risk on the combined-sprint option
strengthen_items.detail: Running all three workstreams in parallel (the combined sprint) assumes sufficient engineering, support, and product bandwidth simultaneously, but no capacity constraint is currently represented, which could make that option appear less costly than it is.

strengthen_items.label: Reframe the goal around ticket volume reduction, not abstract 'best outcome'
strengthen_items.detail: The stated goal is generic; tying it explicitly to the measurable trigger — ticket volume having doubled since March — would make it easier to evaluate whether each option actually closes the gap.

strengthen_items.detail: No status quo option detected — add one to measure improvement. If one of your existing options is the baseline (e.g. 'Continue as-is', 'Maintain current approach'), rename it to make the baseline intent explicit.
